consumption_highway_wh_per_km.notes: Test: 70 mph (113 km/h) steady, 20-35 F (about -7 to 2 C) with headwinds, wheel size not stated, battery-side (car-reported energy) | 2025 Silverado EV LT Extended Range (same dual-motor AWD and Extended pack as our 2026 LT). 179.9 kWh reported by the car over 320.6 mi: 179.9 / 320.6 = 561.1 Wh/mi / 1.609344 = 349 Wh/km. Cold and windy, so well above a mild-weather figure; battery capacity about 182 kWh per the article. Other Silverado test seen (not attached, different pack): Trail Boss Max Range 70 mph, 454 mi, about 2.1 mi/kWh. | NOT FOR CALIBRATION: cold (20-35 F) with headwinds inflate this figure; exclude it from the highway-factor fit (item 3.7).

Test: 70 mph (113 km/h) steady, mid-80s F (~29 C), climate 70 F low fan, wheel size not stated, battery-side (car display) | 2024 Equinox EV FWD 2RS (same generation and 85 kWh pack as our 2026 FWD). Car reported 90.2 kWh used over 303 mi (3.4 mi/kWh): 90.2 kWh / 303 mi = 297.7 Wh/mi / 1.609344 = 185 Wh/km. Hot weather with A/C load. Other tests seen: Consumer Reports AWD 304 mi at 70 mph (no energy figure, paywalled).

Test: 70 mph (113 km/h) steady, upper 60s to ~80 F (about 20-27 C), wheel size not stated, battery-side (vehicle energy gauge) | 2023 Lyriq RWD (same generation; Cadillac-listed usable 102 kWh). 104.7 kWh over 330 mi: 104.7 / 330 = 317.3 Wh/mi / 1.609344 = 197 Wh/km (article says 3.1 mi/kWh). Other test seen: Car and Driver 75 mph, 2023 RWD 20-inch, 270 mi (via Autoblog, no consumption). | Main session: the page calls 102 kWh usable while our data has 95 usable / 100.4 gross, and the gauge read 104.7 kWh used; 2023 to 2026 RWD pack/motor match is plausible but not confirmed.

Test: 70 mph (113 km/h) steady, upper 50s to mid-60s F (about 15-18 C), dry, wheel size not stated, battery-side (car display, not confirmed) | 2023 Mach-E Premium AWD extended range (91 kWh usable; same generation and pack as our 2026 AWD ER). Article reports 3.1 mi/kWh over 285 mi: 1000 / (3.1 x 1.609344) = 200 Wh/km. Other tests seen: 2021 First Edition AWD ER 285 mi; 2021 RWD Route 1 18-inch 287.4 mi (no energy figure). | Main session: 3.1 mi/kWh is a rounded figure (197-204 Wh/km); the page states no kWh total. Our data lists 91 kWh usable.

Test: 70 mph (113 km/h) steady, low 70s to ~80 F (about 22-26 C), wheel size not stated, battery-side (car display, not confirmed) | 2022 Lightning Lariat Extended Range, 131 kWh usable, dual-motor AWD (same pack and generation as our 2025 ER 131 kWh). 2.1 mi/kWh over 270 mi: 1000 / (2.1 x 1.609344) = 296 Wh/km (article: 29.5 kWh/100 km). Other tests seen: Out of Spec Platinum about 258-260 mi on roughly 130 kWh; Consumer Reports Lariat ER 270 mi. | Main session: the page calls 131 kWh usable; our data has 131 gross / 123 usable. Same pack.
